To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have shown that a promoter from a ribosomal RNA gene, which normally is expressed in bloodstream trypanosomes at all times, is efficiently inactivated and activated when placed in the promoter position of an expression site for a VSG gene.
The promoter of a VSG expression site is efficiently replaced by a rDNA promoter and can be switched on and off.

The promoter of a VSG gene expression sites can be replaced with the promoter of the ribosomal DNA (a gene that is normally constitutivly active), and the ribosomal DNA promoter can be efficiently switched off and on in the context of a VSG expression site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
gene expression in the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma (T.) brucei.
the molecular biology of the African trypanosome, which causes sleeping sickness in humans and nagana in cattle.
the molecular mechanisms of gene regulation in the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma (T.) brucei.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

T. bruceis a single-celled eukaryotic organism that is able to change its VSG coat by switching between telomeric expression sites, and that the expression of a given expression site is controlled by an epigenetic silencing mechanism that is not promoter specific.
the rDNA promoter is not a promoter specific for the rDNA, but a promoter that can be used for any gene in the genome, including a gene in a VSG gene expression-site.
VSG gene expression is regulated by a mechanism of epigenetic control that is not specific to the VEG gene promoter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that VSG gene expression in bloodstream-form Trypanosoma can be controlled by an artificial promoter, and that the promoter is subject to the same control as the native VSG promoter.
the rDNA promoter is not specific to VSG expression site.

VSG expression sites can be controlled in bloodstream-form T.brucei by a promoter that is normally active in the rDNA locus, indicating that the mechanism of VSG expression site inactivation is independent of promoter sequence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the VSG expression-site promoter is not essential to the control mechanism.
the VSG gene is regulated by an epigenetic control mechanism.

we have shown that the promoter of a VSG expression site can be replaced by a ribosomal DNA promoter and that the rDNA promoter is efficiently inactivated and activated in the context of a VSG gene expression sites.
